solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hurt someone's feelings in cricket side, by boundary

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field
an end is a limit or boundary

explanation.surface: A player's pride is wounded on the off side, beside the rope at the edge of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the leg side, so OFF is a standard abbreviation for one side.
explanation.definitionFit: To give offence is exactly to wound someone's feelings, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Boy — one's lost a Swiss coin

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so these letters drop out of the name

parts.note: Francis is a boy's name
one is I, plus 's for 'is', giving I and S

explanation.surface: A lad mislays a Swiss coin.
explanation.walkthrough: Read "one's" as "one is": I (the Roman one) plus S, which leave the name Francis.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc is the currency unit used in Switzerland.

clue.text: Former partner, a stud — he could be worn out!

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: says the following letters could be something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman's ex was a stud, and is now tired out from it.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash suggests a pause in a story about a stud; 'could be' is the anagram signal, and the stud's letters join A and HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted and worn out both describe someone utterly tired, simple synonyms.

clue.text: Gloomy pub in Scottish town

parts.note: dun is a dull, dark greyish colour, so gloomy
a bar is a pub or drinking place

explanation.surface: A dreary public house in a town north of the border.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunbar is a coastal town east of Edinburgh in Scotland, an example of the category.

clue.text: Advocate working on treaty

indicators.note: letters that are working are being worked over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A lawyer busy on drafting an international agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: An attorney is a lawyer, and an advocate is one who pleads in court: synonyms.

clue.text: Immediately after a hotpot, had crackers

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone eats crackers straight after a Lancashire stew.
explanation.walkthrough: Hotpot is a British meat-and-potato stew; 'crackers' looks like food in the surface but is the signal to scramble every word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means without hesitation or delay, so it matches immediately.

clue.text: A nettle waving about caught arm

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the scrambled letters surround another
waving suggests movement to and fro, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A stinging plant blowing in the wind brushed against someone's arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waving' turns A NETTLE into TENTALE, and 'about' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tentacle is the flexible limb of an octopus or squid, functioning as an arm.

clue.text: Region supplying genuine drop of malt

parts.note: real means genuine

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, here the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A whisky district providing a real taste of single malt.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a domain or field, so a region of territory or interest.

clue.text: Dream sale excited Hugo's girl?

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A dreamy sale stirs up a girl the writer Hugo admired.
explanation.walkthrough: Esmeralda is the gypsy heroine of Victor Hugo's The Hunchback of Notre-Dame.
explanation.definitionFit: Esmeralda is a famous female character in a novel by Victor Hugo, so a girl of his.

clue.text: Saw nothing untoward in a Tyne and Wear town

indicators.note: untoward means unexpected or improper, so the letters are put awry

explanation.surface: A visitor saw nothing amiss in a north-east English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyne and Wear is a county in north-east England, around Newcastle and Sunderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Washington is a new town in Sunderland's borough, an example of a town in that county.

clue.text: Host, extremely foolish to lose face

indicators.note: losing the face means dropping the front, the first letter

parts.note: barmy is British slang for crazy or very foolish

explanation.surface: A party host so silly they suffer embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a multitude, especially of soldiers, so an army in the old sense.

clue.text: Faithful, a Catholic clergyman

parts.note: a curate is an assistant parish clergyman

explanation.surface: A loyal priest of the Roman church.
explanation.definitionFit: A faithful copy is an accurate one, true to the original.

clue.text: Look up to one in weird dream

indicators.note: the scrambled letters take the numeral inside them
weird means strange, so the letters come out oddly ordered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone admires a person who appeared in a strange dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weird' turns DREAM into ADMRE and 'in' places I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to respect them, the idiom look up to.

clue.text: A flighty creature up to some criminal activity

parts.note: a tit is a small bird, a creature of flight

explanation.surface: A frivolous creature engaged in mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty' looks like a description of character; it means simply able to fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at it is informal for engaged in mischief or wrongdoing again.

clue.text: Where a course at Oxford may take one, up to a point

definitions.text: Where a course at Oxford may take one
definitions.meaning: a university course leads a student towards a qualification

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means as far as a qualification and idiomatically means to some extent.

clue.text: Pudding poorly cooked, left by everybody ultimately

indicators.note: cooked suggests something altered or tampered with, so the letters are rearranged
ultimately points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A badly made dessert abandoned by every diner in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' is the scramble signal, not kitchen work; roly-poly is a British rolled suet pudding with jam.
explanation.definitionFit: Roly-poly is a traditional steamed or baked jam pudding, an example of the category.

clue.text: European nobleman to name an Ivy League university

parts.note: a prince is a ruler or high noble of a European house
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Continental aristocrat lends his name to an American college.
explanation.definitionFit: Princeton in New Jersey is one of the eight Ivy League universities, an example.

clue.text: Bird in hot weather diving into English river

indicators.note: diving into means plunging inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the Wear flows through Durham and Sunderland
a heat or heatwave is a spell of hot weather

explanation.surface: A bird in a heatwave plunges into an English river to cool off.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheatear is a small migratory songbird, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Difficulty encountered in stern on vessel

parts.note: stern means severe or hard
a ship is a sea vessel

explanation.surface: Trouble met at the back of a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' looks like the rear of the vessel, but it is the adjective meaning harsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardship is suffering or adversity, so a difficulty one must endure.

clue.text: I'm a male prayer leader

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe; that the letters also run unbroken through the clue is a coincidence, as the pieces form a charade

explanation.surface: A man introduces himself as the one who leads worship.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads communal prayers in a mosque, a direct description.

clue.text: Ethnic, first in box in court case

indicators.note: this second in places the letter inside the court case

parts.note: a trial is a case heard in court

indicators.note: the first letter in the word

explanation.surface: An ethnic dispute comes first in the witness box at a hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal relates to a tribe or ethnic group, so means ethnic.

clue.text: Outbreak of rabies in part of Europe

indicators.note: an outbreak breaks things up, so the letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Rabies breaks out in a European country.
explanation.definitionFit: Serbia is a Balkan country, so a part of Europe.

clue.text: Writer about to leave house

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: An author is about to move out of a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns NIB into BIN. House is another name for the game, and the cry when a card is full.
explanation.definitionFit: House, or housey-housey, is an old British name for the numbers game.

clue.text: A previous calculation in fathoms coaster at sea required

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fathoms

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A navigator needed an earlier reckoning, measured in fathoms, for a coastal ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' fits the nautical surface but signals a scramble; 'required' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast is a prediction worked out in advance, a calculation made beforehand.

clue.text: Pitch in Oslo, perfect

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words, running across their gap

explanation.surface: A flawless football pitch in the Norwegian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitch can mean the slant of a roof, so a slope or incline.

clue.text: Refuse to have king included in embargo

indicators.note: included in means placed inside another piece

parts.note: a ban is an embargo
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: A monarch is made subject to a trade embargo.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran is husks sifted from flour, so a waste product or refuse.

clue.text: Showing off gift

definitions.meaning: behaving to draw attention, as in making a spectacle of oneself
a grant or scholarship given to a student

explanation.definitionFit: Making a public display of oneself is the first sense; a school or university award is the second.

clue.text: Protest about blackleg, a party member

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
C stands for circa, about
a rat is a strikebreaker or blackleg

explanation.surface: A march against a strikebreaker who belongs to a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackleg is British for a worker who crosses a picket line.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat belongs to the US Democratic Party, so is a member of a party.

clue.text: Leader of gang entering ship to delay departure

indicators.note: entering means going inside the other piece

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A gang boss boards an ocean liner, holding up its sailing.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger is to stay around and be slow in leaving.
